references.text: The Lord predicts that he will perform many signs and wonders in Egypt and strike Egypt with his hand.
Fulfillment of the promise that Pharaoh will send the Israelites out after the plagues.
Moses reminds the people of God's mighty hand and the great wonders he performed in Egypt.
Reference to the signs and wonders the Lord performed against Egypt and Pharaoh.
The Lord brought Israel out of Egypt with a strong hand, signs, and wonders.
Joshua recalls how God struck Egypt with plagues.
Nehemiah refers to the signs and wonders against Pharaoh and all his land.
The psalm describes God's signs and wonders in Egypt and how he struck the Egyptians.
A listing of God's miraculous deeds and plagues in Egypt.
The Lord struck Egypt's firstborn with signs and wonders.
Jeremiah refers to God's signs and wonders in Egypt and his outstretched hand.
Stephen speaks about Moses leading the people out and performing wonders and signs in Egypt.
A direct parallel in the account of the exodus from Egypt where God's hand is stretched out both to judge and to reveal himself.
Direct fulfillment of the threat in Ex 3:20; Ex 12:12 describes the actual execution of judgment against the gods and firstborn of Egypt.
Complementary promises in the same period: Ex 3:20 describes the method of judgment, while Ex 6:7 describes the covenant relationship achieved through deliverance.
